## core
- `core/asset_manifest.gd`: Checks assets/manifest.json: every file under the assets folder (except *.import, .gdignore, *.md and the manifest itself) has an entry with a non-empty source and licence
- `core/audio_director.gd`: All game audio (autoload AudioDirector)
- `core/content_db.gd`: All authored game data (autoload ContentDB)
- `core/defs/def.gd`: Base of every content definition: an id, how it reads itself from JSON, and which other ids it needs
- `core/defs/def_reader.gd`: Typed, validated reads from one JSON object
- `core/defs/flow_rules_def.gd`: Numbers and ids of the game flow (content/prototype/flow.json): the music of exploring and of fighting, how long the player must stand still for a spot to count as safe (the unstuck target), and where the debug labels sit
- `core/event_bus.gd`: Global signals between features (autoload EventBus)
- `core/game_state.gd`: Everything a save file holds (autoload GameState)
- `core/save/router_saves.gd`: Helper for Router save operations: slot checks and file I/O delegates
- `core/save/save_codec.gd`: Pure save format: migrate() lifts any old save dictionary to the current version one step at a time (_v1_to_v2, _v2_to_v3, _v3_to_v4), and sanitize() drops content ids the game no longer knows
- `core/save/save_service.gd`: Save slots on disk: <dir>/slot_N.json, written atomically (tmp file, then rename over the old one, with the previous save kept as slot_N.json.bak)
- `core/scene_router.gd`: Game flow owner (autoload Router): title, new game, save and load, busy state, unstuck, and the play-time clock
- `core/tests/fixtures/assets_bad/a.txt`
- `core/tests/fixtures/assets_bad/manifest.json`: content: ? x0
- `core/tests/fixtures/assets_bad/unlisted.txt`
- `core/tests/fixtures/assets_ok/manifest.json`: content: ? x0
- `core/tests/fixtures/assets_ok/sub/note.txt`
- `core/tests/fixtures/bad_content/combatants.json`: content: combatant x1
- `core/tests/fixtures/bad_text/bad.csv`
- `core/tests/fixtures/bad_text/dup_a.csv`
- `core/tests/fixtures/bad_text/dup_b.csv`
- `core/tests/fixtures/save_v3.json`: content: ? x0
- `core/tests/fixtures/save_v5.json`: content: ? x0
- `core/tests/test_asset_manifest.gd`: Asset manifest: every shipped asset has a source and licence; the checker catches missing entries, empty licences and entries without files (fixtures), and ignores notes, .import files and the manifest
- `core/tests/test_content_db.gd`: The shipped content loads with no problems, and the validator catches broken content
- `core/tests/test_def_reader.gd`: DefReader int lists and cross-key problems, and the encounter definition built on them
- `core/tests/test_game_state.gd`: Save data survives a round trip through JSON, a version-1 save migrates, and an unknown version is refused
- `core/tests/test_save_codec.gd`: SaveCodec: a v3 fixture migrates to v6, unknown versions are refused, unknown content ids are dropped with a warning, the full v4 state (money, bag, vitals with hp 0, cleared patrols) round trips through GameState, and the v5 fixture gains Bilqis's pistol and every hero's ring with nothing else changed
- `core/tests/test_save_service.gd`: SaveService: round trip, summary, an existing slot is replaced (the rename overwrites on Windows too) with the old save kept as .bak, and corrupt files give a clear error
- `core/tests/test_text_db.gd`: Player text: every localization CSV loads, keys translate, and a malformed file is reported
- `core/text_db.gd`: Player text (autoload TextDB): loads every res://localization/*.csv (header "keys,<lang>,...") into the TranslationServer at startup, so tr("KEY") works

## features
- `features/art/defs/clip_def.gd`: The timing of one model clip (an animation of the shared library): its length, whether it loops, and for a one-shot the Hades-style retiming (docs/design/characters-3d.md 4): the clip runs slow to `windup_t`, holds a beat, runs fast through the strike to `strike_end_t` (`impact_t` lands inside it) and eases out
- `features/art/defs/model_def.gd`: One live 3D character model (docs/design/characters-3d.md 5): a skinned glTF (or a rigid model built in code) with its height, footprint, anchors (bone names), the facade state -> ClipDef map, stride and turn speed, skin tint, and the parts it wears
- `features/art/defs/model_part_def.gd`: One part worn by a model on a bone (a "part" of a ModelDef): hair or brows from a glTF, a rigid mesh from a glb (the drone's hull), a garment lathed around the bone's up axis from a radius profile (skirt, coat, head wrap), a sleeve (capsule from the bone to its child), or the grandfather's jambiyah hilt (Rodin grip and sheath scenes)
- `features/art/defs/palette_def.gd`: The locked colour palette: one letter per colour ("." is transparent and never listed here)
- `features/art/defs/sprite_def.gd`: One pixel sprite: rows of palette letters ('.' = transparent), all the same width, feet on the last row
- `features/art/defs/visual_rules_def.gd`: Numbers for how a CharacterVisual looks and moves: art scale, idle breathing, walking (bob, squash and stretch, lean, dust), turning, the blob shadow, and the battle motions (anticipation, lunge with afterimages, recoil, hurt, knocked out, revive, victory hop)
- `features/art/logic/clip_timing.gd`: Pure retiming of a one-shot clip (ClipDef): real seconds <-> clip seconds
- `features/art/logic/locomotion.gd`: Pure walking maths for a model: which gait a ground speed means, the playback rate that keeps feet from sliding (speed / stride), a smoothed speed, the lean into acceleration and the foot contacts a gait loop passes
- `features/art/logic/model_gait.gd`: Pure choice of a model's looping clip: which gait (idle, walk, run) its measured ground speed and the state the facade asked for mean, and the playback rate that keeps its feet on the ground
- `features/art/logic/pixel_art.gd`: Turns a palette-indexed sprite (rows of letters) into an Image or texture
- `features/art/logic/pose_match.gd`: Pure maths of pose retargeting between two humanoid rigs with the same bone names but other bone axes and rest poses (a Rodin body driven by the Quaternius library): a constant per-bone offset so the target bone always points where the source bone points, and the hips' travel scaled from one leg length to the other
- `features/art/logic/yaw_turn.gd`: Pure turning for a model: the yaw (radians, about +y; 0 faces +z) of a ground direction and a capped step toward it that always takes the short way round
- `features/art/tests/test_character_motion.gd`: CharacterVisual motion: the shader material carries the data (minimum light, rim), knocked out / revived snap to the right look, the battle motions and the little effects (dust, afterimages, shadow) run without errors, and the sprite stays crisp (nearest filtering)
- `features/art/tests/test_model_defs.gd`: The data behind the offline sprite sources (content/art/models.json, clips.json) against the imported assets: every model maps all nine states to clips that exist, every clip names a real animation of the shared library with its length and an impact inside it, the bodies keep the rig's bone names, and every anchor and part bone resolves
- `features/art/tests/test_model_logic.gd`: The pure maths behind live 3D characters: ClipTiming (wind-up, hold, strike, recovery and the events on that curve), Locomotion (gait, stride to playback rate, lean, foot contacts passed) and YawTurn (the capped short-way turn)
- `features/art/tests/test_model_source.gd`: The live 3D source behind the CharacterVisual facade: the model is built and painted, clips announce impact and end on the retimed curve (and wait for the hit pause), the body turns by yaw and never by a negative scale, the feet pace the ground and sound a footstep on each foot contact, a knocked-out body stays down, the grandfather's hilt is drawn for a strike and sheathed after, and a CharacterVisual without a model def falls back to the pixel sprite
- `features/art/tests/test_pose_match.gd`: Retargeting (PoseMatch, PoseFollow): the swing turns one direction into another, the per-bone offset makes the target bone point where the source bone points (at rest and after a turn), the hips travel scales with hip height, and a pose_source model's body follows its hidden source (Zayd's Rodin model stands up with the hand below the head); mirrored, the other arm does the move (Zayd's cast raises his prosthetic right arm)
- `features/art/tests/test_rodin_parts.gd`: Feras's Rodin pieces after tools/rodin: Zayd's baked dagger is pressed flat onto his chest (the code hilt is his only jambiyah), the grandfather's hilt is the Rodin grip above the belt origin and the Rodin sheath below it curving forward (the blade stays the code one), and the survey drone's hull is the Rodin mesh at hover height
- `features/art/tests/test_sprites.gd`: Prototype T7: every sprite is well formed and uses only palette letters; PixelArt and CharacterVisual work
- `features/art/tests/test_visual_anchors.gd`: purpose: Every body-anchor share is read from content/art/visual.json, and a missing key is a content error
- `features/art/tests/test_visual_contract.gd`: The CharacterVisual contract: play(state, facing), the anchors, clip events, the pixel and puppet sources behind the facade, and the pulse flag that switches the whole-body squash off for puppets
- `features/art/view/character.gdshader`
- `features/art/view/character_fx.gd`: The small effects around one CharacterVisual: a soft blob shadow on the floor, dust puffs at the feet and the fading afterimages of a lunge
- `features/art/view/character_ghost.gdshader`
- `features/art/view/character_hull.gdshader`
- `features/art/view/character_motion.gd`: The root moves of a CharacterVisual: they slide `root` and nothing else (the picture and its squash belong to the VisualSource)
- `features/art/view/character_skin.gdshader`
- `features/art/view/character_visual.gd`: A character standing in the 3D world (feet on the node's origin): the facade the game talks to
- `features/art/view/garment_mesh.gd`: Stand-in clothing built in code from a ModelPartDef (until Feras's own models): a lathe (a skirt, a coat, a head wrap) turned from a radius profile, and `prim`, which adds a coloured primitive to a SurfaceTool so a whole prop (the jambiyah) is one mesh with vertex colours (the skin shader multiplies COLOR into the albedo)
- `features/art/view/hilt_mesh.gd`: The stand-in for Zayd's grandfather's jambiyah (Heirloom `grandfather_hilt`), built in code from the part's colours until Feras's picture becomes a model: a curved horn grip with two silver bands, a T pommel with a carnelian stone, a curved blade, and a curved leather sheath with silver throat and tip
- `features/art/view/hilt_parts.gd`: The grandfather's jambiyah as nodes (the part's Rodin grip and sheath scenes, else HiltMesh's stand-in; the blade is always HiltMesh's): a sheath and the hilt with its blade sit at the belt (`root`); draw() carries the hilt to the hand bone for a strike (the blade shows, the sheath stays), sheathe() puts it back
- `features/art/view/model_anchors.gd`: purpose: A live model's body anchors from its own height and width, with every share read from visual.json
- `features/art/view/model_clips.gd`: Drives a MANUAL AnimationPlayer
- `features/art/view/model_materials.gd`: The materials of live 3D characters: every surface (body, eyes, brows, hair, garments, the hilt) is a ShaderMaterial of character_skin.gdshader, so the painted light of the look reaches all of them through `materials()` (the baker's light sets their uniforms), and one `set_all` call drives the flash, desat and glow of the whole character
- `features/art/view/model_move.gd`: What a model's body does on the ground: the ground speed it is really moving at (measured from its own position, so animation and feet agree whoever moves it), the yaw it eases toward at the model's turn speed, and the lean into an acceleration
- `features/art/view/model_parts.gd`: Puts one ModelPartDef on a rig: hair or a rigid mesh from its glTF, a lathed garment, a sleeve capsule or the jambiyah, each on a BoneAttachment3D so it follows the bone through every animation
- `features/art/view/model_react.gd`: What a live 3D character does in answer to the battle's cues, on its materials and on `visual.body`: the hit flash, the revive glow, the knocked-out tint, the small squash of a hit (squash lives on the facade's body node, never on bones) and the victory hop
- `features/art/view/model_rig.gd`: Builds one skinned character under a holder node from its ModelDef: the glTF body (scaled to height_m), its painted materials, the parts it wears on BoneAttachment3D nodes, and a MANUAL AnimationPlayer that carries the shared Quaternius animation library (the same 65-bone rig as the stand-in bodies; a body with other bone axes names a `pose_source` that plays the clips hidden and PoseFollow retargets; the library scene is loaded once and only its AnimationLibrary is kept)
- `features/art/view/model_source.gd`: The live 3D source of a CharacterVisual (docs/design/characters-3d.md): a skinned model (ModelRig) or a rigid one (RigidRig) from the ModelDef with the sprite's id
- `features/art/view/model_weapon.gd`: The grandfather's jambiyah in use: drawn from the belt into the hand when a strike begins (the weapon trail starts tracking its hilt and its point), an arc smear on the impact frame, sheathed and the trail released when the clip ends
- `features/art/view/node_scan.gd`: Finds nodes inside an imported scene by walking its children: every node of a class (the skeleton, the meshes) and the chain of nodes from the root down to one of them (to multiply their transforms)
- `features/art/view/painted_light.gdshaderinc`
- `features/art/view/pixel_motion.gd`: The body-shape motions of a pixel character (PixelSource): whole-body squash and stretch (`pulse`), the cast crouch, the victory hop, the hit flash, knocked out and revive
- `features/art/view/pixel_source.gd`: The pixel-art source of a CharacterVisual (today's look, unchanged): a lit, billboarded quad with the sprite's texture (nearest filtering), idle breathing, the walk bob with squash and stretch, the lean into the move and dust at the feet
- `features/art/view/pose_follow.gd`: Retargets at run time: a hidden source body with the library's rig plays the clips, and every frame each target bone of the same name takes the source bone's model-space rotation times a constant offset (PoseMatch), so a body with other bone axes and rest pose (Feras's Rodin models) moves like the library
- `features/art/view/rigid_rig.gd`: A model that is not skinned: a few rigid parts moved by code (the survey drone: its Rodin hull)
- `features/art/view/visual_source.gd`: What draws a CharacterVisual
- `features/art/view/weapon_smear.gdshader`
- `features/art/view/weapon_trail.gd`: The weapon's swing in the air: a ribbon between two tracked points (hilt and the blade's point) that fades along its age, and an arc smear card (a crescent) flashed on the strike frame
- `features/audio/defs/audio_rules_def.gd`: Mixer and behaviour numbers of the AudioDirector (content/audio/rules.json): bus volumes, voice pools, music fade and duck, hit weight, text blip rate, item chime boost per rarity, and which sound each move uses
- `features/audio/defs/music_def.gd`: One music track (content/audio/music.json): its file, volume, whether it loops, and an optional fallback track
- `features/audio/defs/screen_music_def.gd`: Maps one screen id (from the Screens stack) to the music track id it plays while open
- `features/audio/defs/sound_def.gd`: One sound effect (content/audio/sounds.json): file variants (one is picked each play), the bus it plays on, its volume, a random pitch range so repeats differ and whether it ducks the music (stingers)
- `features/audio/logic/music_logic.gd`: Pure rules for music playback: fallback resolution when audio files are missing, and mapping screen ids
- `features/audio/logic/music_stack.gd`: Pure stack of open screen ids deciding which music track plays (content/audio/screen_music.json)
- `features/audio/logic/sound_logic.gd`: Pure sound rules: which variant to play, which sound a move uses and the item chime boost for a rarity
- `features/audio/tests/test_audio.gd`: Audio: every sound and music entry is well formed, every sfx file exists, every vfx id has a sound, the pure sound rules hold, and the AudioDirector builds its buses, plays headless and skips missing music
- `features/audio/tests/test_music_choices.gd`: The owner's music choices (DECISIONS 2026-10-22): menus and the herb stall keep the area music (no screen maps them), every patrol names one of the three battle themes and all three are used, and every track's file exists
- `features/audio/tests/test_music_contexts.gd`: Tests for music contexts: pure stack resolution across all branches, missing file fallback resolution, validation of screen_music definitions, pause process mode, and track resume positions
- `features/audio/tests/test_sound_ids.gd`: Sound ids: every id the code asks the AudioDirector for exists in sounds.json with existing files, and the synthesized Arc Discharge files are 44.1 kHz mono, 0.6-0.9 s long and peak under -1 dBFS
- `features/audio/view/music_deck.gd`: The music side of the AudioDirector: two players so one track crossfades into the next, a duck under stingers, and a pure stack of screen music contexts (content/audio/screen_music.json)
- `features/combat/defs/action_def.gd`: One battle technique: its cost, power, who it targets, and what it does to the timeline (cast speed, recovery, knockback, cancel)
- `features/combat/defs/battle_rules_def.gd`: The tunable numbers of one battle ruleset: damage and heal formula factors, SP gain, the stall guard, start ranges and the two thresholds BattleAI uses for heals and guards
- `features/combat/defs/battle_view_def.gd`: Layout and pacing numbers of the battle screen (content/combat/view.json): camera, where each formation slot stands, ticks per frame, hit-stop and banner times, floating-text sizes, HUD sizes and colours
- `features/combat/defs/combatant_def.gd`: One kind of fighter (a party member or an enemy type): base stats and the actions it can use
- `features/combat/defs/encounter_def.gd`: One battle setup: which enemies stand in which formation slots, which slots the party takes, and the guaranteed rewards (equippable loot ids, riyal and consumables, no randomness) granted after a win, and its music
- `features/combat/defs/status_def.gd`: One status effect: how long it lasts and how it changes timeline speed, interrupt immunity and the damage the afflicted unit takes (guarded: 0.6 means 40% less)
- `features/combat/defs/vfx_def.gd`: One battle effect kind (content/combat/vfx.json, id = an ActionDef.VFX_KINDS entry): when the hit lands, the hitstop and camera shake / push it earns, and the layers of pooled sprites it paints
- `features/combat/defs/vfx_layer.gd`: One layer of a VfxDef: `count` sprites of one texture that start at an anchor (plus an offset), grow from size to size_end, drift or travel, spin and fade
- `features/combat/harness/balance.gd`: Balance harness: seeded battles per gear pairing with BattleAI playing both sides, one table
- `features/combat/harness/battle_loader.gd`: Gathers the battle content from a loaded ContentDB and builds ready-to-run BattleSims for the default encounter
- `features/combat/harness/item_policy.gd`: The balance harness's opt-in herb use (docs/design/economy.md section 9): a white herb on a downed hero, a pink herb on the living hero below 40% HP, a yellow herb when a hero cannot pay for his cheapest move
- `features/combat/harness/party_builder.gd`: Fills GearStates and builds hero fighters / parties from saved equipment or a GameState through one BattleLoader's content dictionaries (used through BattleLoader's hero_from_state / party_* delegates)
- `features/combat/logic/battle_action_rules.gd`: Move uses per battle, miss roll for confused units, and status cures for BattleSim and BattleResolver
- `features/combat/logic/battle_ai.gd`: The one battle policy (enemies in play, both sides in the balance harness), in this order: 1
- `features/combat/logic/battle_ai_tactics.gd`: Tactics evaluation for BattleAI (section 4): stance against incoming melee, shove near COMMAND, arc on spread/jammed
- `features/combat/logic/battle_flee_logic.gd`: Flee resolution logic, extracted to keep battle_sim.gd under 200 lines
- `features/combat/logic/battle_items.gd`: The Items command of a battle (docs/design/economy.md section 5)
- `features/combat/logic/battle_outcome.gd`: What a finished battle hands back: result (victory, defeat, retry, load, title), the party's vitals and bag after the fight, and the rewards (money, equippable items, consumables) still to be applied to GameState by the Router
- `features/combat/logic/battle_request.gd`: What the Router hands to a battle: encounter, arena, ambush, seed, party order, and the pre-battle snapshot (vitals, bag, money) that "Retry fight" restores
- `features/combat/logic/battle_resolver.gd`: Resolves one landed act (docs/design/combat.md, "Resolving an action"): targets, damage or heal per target, timeline effect per hit, status, SP gain, regen, status turns
- `features/combat/logic/battle_rolls.gd`: Pure roll calculations (no timeline dependency): hit, crit, resist, flee
- `features/combat/logic/battle_setup.gd`: Everything BattleSim.create_from needs for one fight, in one object: the built party (in party order, one CombatantDef per hero) and the enemies with their formation slots, the rules and move tables, the carried vitals and bag, the gear snapshot, the seed, the ambush, which encounter and arena, and the stage anchor
- `features/combat/logic/battle_sim.gd`: One battle (docs/design/combat.md): builds the units, steps the Timeline one tick at a time, asks the player (heroes) or BattleAI (enemies) for choices, resolves acts and decides victory or defeat
- `features/combat/logic/battle_sim_runner.gd`: Step loop logic extracted to keep battle_sim.gd under 200 lines
- `features/combat/logic/battle_targets.gd`: Who can do what in a battle: a unit's moves, which of them it can pay for, and who a move may target
- `features/combat/logic/formation.gd`: Two rows per side: slots 0-1 are the vanguard, 2-3 the rearguard, and slot n+2 stands behind slot n
- `features/combat/logic/hud_layout.gd`: Pure screen-rectangle maths for the battle HUD: the box around projected points, where a panel may sit beside a fighter without covering any fighter, which fighter the mouse points at, and how an info card fades
- `features/combat/logic/item_action.gd`: A consumable as a battle cast: an ActionDef built from a ConsumableDef, so the timeline treats it like any move (cast speed, recovery, the cast bar, interrupts)
- `features/combat/logic/timeline.gd`: Grandia-style initiative track (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, "Combat")
- `features/combat/logic/timeline_event.gd`: One thing that happened in a battle, for the battle view and logs: what, who, a value (timeline position, damage, status turns) and a detail id (the action for damage, the status for status/status_ended)
- `features/combat/logic/unit_letters.gd`: Tells apart units of the same kind on one side: two Concession Enforcers are A and B, a lone unit has no letter
- `features/combat/logic/unit_state.gd`: One fighter during one battle: the numbers that change (hp, timeline position, the action being cast), built from a read-only CombatantDef
- `features/combat/tests/battle_probe.gd`: Test helper (not a test): hand-made fighters, moves and battles with exact numbers, and loops that play a BattleSim until an event kind appears
- `features/combat/tests/fake_clip_source.gd`: A stand-in VisualSource for battle view tests: a model-like source of a known size that sends clip events only when the test says so, and records what the battle asked of it (clips, facings, hit pauses, collapses)
- `features/combat/tests/test_abu_nabil_balance.gd`: Balance harness for Abu Nabil duel: 200 seeded battles with policy AI on both sides
- `features/combat/tests/test_abu_nabil_combat.gd`: Abu Nabil combat rules: miss rolls for confused units, status cures, uses per battle, and boss AI policy
- `features/combat/tests/test_abu_nabil_spar.gd`: Abu Nabil Spar tests: practice BattleRequest flags, reverse_stab suppression on duels, snapshot restoration on win/loss with zero payout, and retry keeping the chosen opening
- `features/combat/tests/test_action_def.gd`: ActionDef new fields: target, heal, revive, vfx (validated on load), and the shipped actions: every one has a vfx from the agreed list, and the tech moves have the shape the design asks for
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_ai_support.gd`: BattleAI with support moves: heal an ally under 40% HP, revive the fallen, guard before a big enemy cast, and never waste a heal or buff when nobody needs it
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_flow.gd`: How a fight starts: carried vitals fill the units, and a hero with no entry starts full
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_interrupt.gd`: T4: a cancel move landing on a casting enemy interrupts it (back to INTERRUPT_POS) inside BattleSim
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_items.gd`: The Items command in the sim: a herb is reserved when chosen (two heroes cannot share the last one), cast at its cast speed, consumed at ACT with the real amounts, and refunded when the target is no longer valid, when the cast is cut, or when the user falls first
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_menu_support.gd`: The command menu with tech moves: an ally move lists the allies (not the foes), self and all-moves skip the target list and commit at once, and the party is built from saved gear
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_outcome.gd`: The battle contract: BattleSetup carries carried vitals and the bag into units, hero ids come from the party list, BattleOutcome reports vitals after (a downed hero stands at ko_stand_hp after a victory only) and the bag, and the speed / melee numbers come from the battle rules
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_perks.gd`: Perks in battle (sp_per_act, hp_regen, start_bonus, bonus_knockback), Perks.apply on a fighter copy, and the rarity rule that only Rare and above may carry a perk
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_rolls.gd`: Battle rolls: hit, crit, resist, flee formulas at clamps and middle values
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_rules.gd`: T5: damage, SP, cover, retargeting and status turns follow docs/design/combat.md
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_sim.gd`: BattleSim: unit ids, determinism (T1), every battle ends (T2), refused choices, event order, stall guard
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_start.gd`: Starting positions and ambushes, the first-hit-only knockback bonus, downed units, and lands_before()
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_status.gd`: T5 (statuses): applied by a move, refreshed on re-apply, one turn lost per act of the afflicted unit, and the cast-speed / knockback-bonus numbers of a CombatantDef
- `features/combat/tests/test_battle_tech.gd`: Tech moves: ally / self / all-target moves, heals (never above max HP, downed allies stay down unless the move revives), the guarded and overclocked statuses, and the damage-taken multiplier
- `features/combat/tests/test_flee.gd`: Flee: chance, refusal on boss, interrupted flee, FLED outcome rules
- `features/combat/tests/test_formation.gd`: Formation rows: cover and melee multipliers
- `features/combat/tests/test_hud_layout.gd`: HudLayout (pure rect maths) and UnitLetters: boxes around points, panels that dodge fighters, which fighter the mouse points at, the info card's fade, and the A / B letters of same-kind units
- `features/combat/tests/test_item_policy.gd`: ItemPolicy (balance harness): herbs only when the bag has them, deterministic, battles still end
- `features/combat/tests/test_reverse_stab.gd`: The reverse stab: only when the party was ambushed, Zayd strikes the lowest-slot living enemy first
- `features/combat/tests/test_timeline.gd`: Timeline rules: command pause, cast and act, interrupts, knockback limits, determinism
- `features/combat/tests/test_zayd_kit.gd`: Tests for Zayd's redesigned kit (zayd-moves.md section 5 and brief): damage split, sp_gain, after_act_pos, cast_status, bonus vs status, poised counter, shove, and content comparisons
- `features/combat/view/battle_command_menu.gd`: The compact command menu (in the turn panel, beside the hero) for the hero waiting at COMMAND: first one Button per move (unaffordable ones disabled; name, SP cost, a "cancels" / target tag; the focused move's description below), then one Button per valid target (foes or allies; self and all-moves skip this list)
- `features/combat/view/battle_flee_button.gd`: Helper to build the FLEE command-menu button (extracted to keep battle_command_menu.gd under 200 lines)
- `features/combat/view/battle_menu_chips.gd`: The small tags on the right edge of a command-menu button: SP cost (cyan), "cancels" (magenta), the target scope of a self / all move, and for a target the HP and a "will interrupt" warning
- `features/combat/view/battle_style.gd`: Small builders for the battle screen's look (labels, bars, names, head icons)
- `features/combat/view/battle_timeline_bar.gd`: The thin top bar of the battle: a slim brass track from 0 to ACT_POINT with a COMMAND mark and a tinted cast zone (BattleTrackArt, compact), one small head icon per living unit at its timeline position (foes above the track, the party below it), and at the left the name of the chosen target
- `features/combat/view/battle_timeline_ghost.gd`: Ghost landing marker on the timeline bar for previewing knockback (section 3 and 6)
- `features/combat/view/battle_track_art.gd`: The painted brass track of the timeline bar: dark glass, brass rails, tick marks, the tinted cast zone, a gypsum zigzag frieze along the bottom, the COMMAND mark (a brass line with diamonds) and an end cap at ACT
- `features/combat/view/vfx_sprite.gd`: One pooled effect quad
- `features/combat/view/vfx_sprite.gdshader`
- `features/combat/view/vfx_textures.gd`: Procedurally painted effect textures (no files): crisp hard-edged pixel shapes (a bright core and a darker rim, one-bit alpha) plus one soft glow
- `features/debug/playtest/logic/playtest_dump.gd`: purpose: The JSON record of one playtest capture: time, scene, game state, the recent log and the note
- `features/debug/playtest/logic/playtest_log_ring.gd`: purpose: The newest engine log lines of a playtest capture, capped so a long session stays small
- `features/debug/playtest/logic/playtest_marks.gd`: purpose: Stamps a capture's strokes onto the screenshot as square marks one pixel apart along every segment
- `features/debug/playtest/logic/playtest_strokes.gd`: purpose: The strokes of one playtest capture: freehand and ellipse paths in overlay space, with undo
- `features/debug/playtest/playtest_canvas.gd`: purpose: Draws a capture's strokes in red and records left-drag freehand and right-drag ellipse strokes
- `features/debug/playtest/playtest_capture.gd`: purpose: F12 playtest capture: grabs the screen, lets Feras circle bugs and write a note, then saves shot.png, marked.png and state.json under inbox/playtest for Claude to read
- `features/debug/playtest/playtest_capture.tscn`: scene
- `features/debug/playtest/playtest_logger.gd`: purpose: Catches engine errors and warnings into the capture's log ring without printing anything
- `features/debug/playtest/tests/test_playtest_canvas.gd`: purpose: PlaytestCanvas turns real mouse drags into marks: a left drag shows while drawn and is kept on release, a right drag keeps a clean ellipse inside its box (no line back to the corner where the drag began)
- `features/debug/playtest/tests/test_playtest_capture.gd`: purpose: PlaytestCapture pauses while it is open, cancels back to the previous pause state after the input is released, and saves shot.png, marked.png and state.json from an injected grab
- `features/debug/playtest/tests/test_playtest_dump.gd`: purpose: PlaytestDump builds the capture record with every key, plain JSON values, the note/log/event caps and a Windows-safe folder name
- `features/debug/playtest/tests/test_playtest_logger.gd`: purpose: PlaytestLogger records engine errors and error messages into its ring, ignores plain messages, and the ring keeps only the newest lines
- `features/debug/playtest/tests/test_playtest_marks.gd`: purpose: PlaytestMarks paints a stroke onto the screenshot through the capture transform, leaves pixels away from it untouched, dots a lone point and clips points outside the image
- `features/debug/playtest/tests/test_playtest_strokes.gd`: purpose: PlaytestStrokes keeps freehand and ellipse strokes, undo drops only the last, and an ellipse is closed and inside the box it was dragged over
- `features/dialogue/defs/dialogue_choice.gd`: A player choice at the end of a dialogue line: text key, next dialogue (or "end"), and effects
- `features/dialogue/defs/dialogue_def.gd`: A conversation: an ordered list of lines (speaker, expression, text key)
- `features/dialogue/defs/dialogue_line.gd`: One spoken line: who says it, with which expression, localization key, and optional choices
- `features/dialogue/defs/dialogue_style_def.gd`: Look and timing of the dialogue box (fractions of the screen, pixels, colours, speed) and the pixel marks (brows, mouth) that make the stand-in portraits show an expression
- `features/dialogue/defs/speaker_def.gd`: One speaking character: name key, name colour, the pixel sprite id, and where the face sits on that sprite (sprite pixels)
- `features/dialogue/defs/talk_def.gd`: Maps a place id to its first dialogue, after-battle dialogue and ordered chats
- `features/dialogue/dialogue_effects.gd`: Applies side effects from dialogue choices: set_flag, open_shop, start_battle, give_item
- `features/dialogue/logic/dialogue_run.gd`: Steps through a DialogueDef one line at a time
- `features/dialogue/logic/standin_portrait.gd`: Builds a stand-in portrait Image for a speaker without painted art: a soft glow in the speaker colour, a disc in that colour and brow and mouth marks per expression
- `features/dialogue/logic/talk_picker.gd`: Pure picker that selects the next dialogue for a talk place from saved flags: 1
- `features/dialogue/tests/test_abu_nabil_haggle.gd`: Abu Nabil Haggle and Shop tests: Haggle dialogue branches A/B/C/D, flag side effects, walk-away safety, win dialogue, post-win menu gating, and shop prices before/after win
- `features/dialogue/tests/test_dialogue.gd`: Dialogue: T8 (every line has a known speaker, one of 4 expressions, a translating text key), DialogueRun stepping, the object-list reader, the stand-in portraits, and DialogueBox playing to the end once
- `features/dialogue/tests/test_dialogue_choices.gd`: Dialogue choices test: DialogueChoice def parsing, DialogueRun choice exposure and advance blocking, DialogueEffects execution, and DialogueBox button selection
- `features/dialogue/tests/test_dialogue_effects.gd`: Dialogue effects: the start_battle effect asks the battle host through EventBus instead of starting a stage
- `features/dialogue/tests/test_dialogue_v2.gd`: Dialogue v2 (Hades II style): nameplate with epithet, typed text, portrait slide on a speaker change, Cease, the layout sizes from the UI style, and stand-in portraits that no longer touch sprite pixels
- `features/dialogue/tests/test_talk_defs.gd`: Checks that talks.json is well formed and all referenced dialogue ids exist in ContentDB
- `features/dialogue/tests/test_talk_picker.gd`: Tests for TalkPicker: first dialogue, after-battle dialogue on victory, chat sequence and wrapping, battle interruption resuming chats, and defensive fallbacks
- `features/dialogue/view/dialogue_box.gd`: The dialogue box, Hades II style: a big portrait slides in when the speaker changes, a nameplate sits on the box, lines are typed out, and choice buttons offer branching dialogue
- `features/dialogue/view/dialogue_choice_list.gd`: Manages the focusable button list for dialogue choices
- `features/dialogue/view/dialogue_demo.gd`: Manual check: plays the workshop_first dialogue over a plain background (F6 in the editor)
- `features/dialogue/view/dialogue_demo.tscn`: scene
- `features/dialogue/view/dialogue_layout.gd`: Builds the dialogue box's controls in code (Hades II style; sizes from the UI style, laid out for 1920x1080): a big portrait at the left that slides in, an ornate glass text box at the bottom right with a frieze, a nameplate tab on the box's top edge (name in brass, epithet under it) and the button hints
- `features/dialogue/view/portraits.gd`: Finds the portrait texture for (speaker, expression): res://assets/portraits/<speaker>_<expression>.png when it exists (loaded straight from the file, the "keep" importer needs no import step), else the speaker's painted neutral (a painted face beats a stand-in), else a stand-in disc with the expression's brows and mouth (StandinPortrait)
- `features/equipment/defs/hologram_2d_def.gd`: purpose: Anchor points of a 2D menu hologram as fractions of its rect (0..1 from the left and the top)
- `features/equipment/logic/equipment_options.gd`: Pure rules of the equipment screen: which slots a hero has, which OWNED items fit a slot (best rarity first), which items a hero wears now, the fighter built from a staged set of items, and writing a staged set into the saved equipment through Inventory.equip
- `features/equipment/tests/test_equipment.gd`: purpose: Tests the pure EquipmentOptions rules (owned items only, rarer first, per hero and slot)
- `features/equipment/tests/test_equipment_layout.gd`: purpose: Tests EquipmentMenu layout rects, header label widths, and connector lines
- `features/equipment/tests/test_equipment_menu.gd`: purpose: Tests EquipmentMenu layout, 2D hologram stage, slot boxes, equipping, preview and focus
- `features/equipment/tests/test_equipment_new_slots.gd`: purpose: The gear-slots menu tests: Bilqis's frame and barrel boxes, the accessory box and its sockets, and equipping through the new slots
- `features/equipment/tests/test_equipment_polish.gd`: purpose: Tests equipment polish features: hologram override, slot box name/dim ring, stats header, hero header Lv 1
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_boxes.gd`: purpose: Manages the 8 equipment slot boxes, their positions, visibility per hero and focus navigation
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_data.gd`: purpose: What the equipment screen needs from ContentDB, read once
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_desc_bar.gd`: purpose: Description bar (1760x90 at 80,900) showing item name, rarity, description and combat effect
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_detail.gd`: The right-hand side of the equipment screen: the focused item (name in its rarity colour, tag, text, perk and the tech moves it teaches) above the stat comparison (base, with the staged kit, an up / down arrow)
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_hero_header.gd`: purpose: Hero info box (500x140 at 80,124) with portrait bust, name, class, Lv N, and HP/SP/XP bars
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_item_button.gd`: Builds one owned item as a menu button: its name in the rarity colour, the rarity tag and an "Equipped" mark on the right
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_menu.gd`: purpose: Equipment menu with Neon sprite hologram hero, slot boxes, owned list, stats comparison and tabs
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_owned_list.gd`: purpose: Owned items panel (420x620 at 80,260) populated with ListRows and worn "E" chips
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_stats_panel.gd`: purpose: Stats preview panel (440x560) showing now vs after comparison and derived battle rolls
- `features/equipment/view/equipment_tabs_bar.gd`: purpose: Shared top bar (1760x64 at 80,40) with the screen title and the Equipment / Items / Map tabs
- `features/equipment/view/grid_disc.gdshader`
- `features/equipment/view/hologram.gdshader`
- `features/equipment/view/hologram_sprite.gd`: purpose: The still a 2D menu hologram shows: a hero's Neon idle sprite facing the camera, or their portrait
- `features/equipment/view/hologram_stage.gd`: purpose: 800x760 menu hologram: the hero's Neon idle sprite (or portrait) with leader lines to the slot boxes
- `features/equipment/view/slot_box.gd`: purpose: 150x150 equipment slot box showing slot label, item icon or gemstone sockets
- `features/equipment/view/slot_socket_draw.gd`: purpose: Draws socket border and stone icon for gemstone slots in equipment boxes
- `features/items/defs/accessory_def.gd`: A ring any hero can wear (content/items/accessories.json)
- `features/items/defs/armor_def.gd`: Armor worn in slot "<hero>.armor": raises HP, DEF, alters AGI and WT (content/items/armor.json)
- `features/items/defs/chest_def.gd`: A chest holding an equippable (an id of a hilt, blade or prosthetic), riyal and/or consumables; at least one
- `features/items/defs/consumable_def.gd`: A stackable item used from the bag, in the field or in battle (feathered herbs, the qishr cup)
- `features/items/defs/count_map.gd`: Reads an optional {"id": count} JSON object (rewards, the start bag) as {StringName: int}, each count 1 or more
- `features/items/defs/economy_rules_def.gd`: The money and rest numbers (content/economy/rules.json, id "default"): start purse and bag, the cap, the repeat-win payout share, the HP a downed hero stands up with after a victory, the patrol respawn guards
- `features/items/defs/equip_def.gd`: Shared base of everything a hero can wear or wield (hilt, blade, prosthetic): names, a rarity tier and an optional perk (Rare and above only; rules in docs/design/prosthetics.md)
- `features/items/defs/material_def.gd`: purpose: Defines a crafting or upgrade material with rarity and display information
- `features/items/defs/perk_def.gd`: One perk an item can carry: a kind that battle logic implements and an amount
- `features/items/defs/pistol_def.gd`: One part of Bilqis's rivet pistol (content/items/pistols.json): a frame (the grip: agility, cast speed, weight and an optional granted move, like a hilt) or a barrel (attack, knockback, weight, like a blade)
- `features/items/defs/rarity_def.gd`: One rarity tier: its name, display colour, sort order, whether it is story-only (never loot) and whether gear of this tier may carry a perk
- `features/items/defs/shop_def.gd`: A stall: who keeps it, her greeting and the consumable ids on sale (price and sell come from the ConsumableDef)
- `features/items/item_service.gd`: Uses a consumable on the party outside battle against GameState: FieldUse does the rules on copies, this writes the bag and the carried vitals back only when the use worked
- `features/items/logic/accessory.gd`: Pure rules for ring gem sockets: which stones fit a ring
- `features/items/logic/bag.gd`: The party's stackable consumables: counts per id plus RESERVATIONS made by pending battle casts
- `features/items/logic/chests.gd`: Chest rules: opening gives the item once, and the opened state is a saved flag
- `features/items/logic/field_use.gd`: Using a consumable outside battle, pure: the item must be usable in the field, aimed at living allies, and must change something (a full hero is refused)
- `features/items/logic/gear.gd`: Builds a hero's fighter from base stats, class level growth, armor, weapons, prosthetic, socketed gemstones, item upgrades, and perks
- `features/items/logic/gear_state.gd`: Holds all worn gear (weapons, armor, prosthetic, accessory ring), progression level, socketed stones (the hilt's and the ring's), upgrades, and perks for building a hero fighter
- `features/items/logic/holdings.gd`: What rewards are paid into: riyal, the consumable Bag, the unique-item inventory and the flags
- `features/items/logic/inventory.gd`: Which unique items the party owns and whether a hero may wear one in a slot
- `features/items/logic/item_effect.gd`: What a consumable does to one hero: gains() computes the real change from current numbers (never past the maximum, a herb never helps a downed hero, a white herb only a downed one); apply() writes it into carried vitals
- `features/items/logic/perks.gd`: Applies perks to a fighter
- `features/items/logic/pistol.gd`: The hero who carries the rivet pistol: the frame and barrel slots exist for this combatant only (the mirror of Jambiyah.WIELDER for the jambiyah pair)
- `features/items/logic/reward_result.gd`: What a reward really changed: riyal added (after the cap), the equippables that were new, the consumables that fit in the bag, and riyal that came from herbs which did not fit (sold at their sell price)
- `features/items/logic/rewards.gd`: Rewards for a won battle or an opened chest, paid straight into a Holdings
- `features/items/logic/shop.gd`: The herb stall's rules, pure: buy (refused when the stock lacks it, the purse is short or the stack is full) and sell (bag consumables only, never reserved ones; gear is not a consumable so it can never be sold)
- `features/items/logic/shop_result.gd`: What one buy or sell did (or why it did not): reason is &"" on success, else one of Shop.SHORT_MONEY etc
- `features/items/logic/vitals.gd`: Carried HP and SP per hero: {hero id: {"hp": int, "sp": int}}
- `features/items/reward_applier.gd`: Pays rewards (Rewards) into GameState and announces them: item_obtained per new equippable, item_gained per herb stack, money_changed for the riyal
- `features/items/shop_service.gd`: Runs the stall against GameState: Shop does the rules on a Holdings copy, this takes the copy back and announces it
- `features/items/tests/fixtures/bad_items/hilts.json`: content: hilt x3
- `features/items/tests/fixtures/bad_items/rarities.json`: content: rarity x2
- `features/items/tests/test_accessories.gd`: Rings (accessories): socket counts follow rarity (Common 1 
- `features/items/tests/test_bag.gd`: Bag: stack caps with overflow, removal, and reservations (two heroes cannot both claim the last herb; release gives the claim back; consume uses it up)
- `features/items/tests/test_inventory.gd`: Inventory (unique owned items, equip checks per slot), chests (open once, saved flag) and the item_obtained signal on the EventBus
- `features/items/tests/test_items.gd`: Rarity tiers and the shipped items: six tiers with the owner's colours, every equippable has a real rarity, ids are unique across hilts / blades / prosthetics, the Heirloom is story-only and never loot, and bad content (an unknown rarity, a bad colour) is reported
- `features/items/tests/test_pistols.gd`: Bilqis's rivet pistol: the frame merges like a hilt, the barrel like a blade; both fit only their wielder; the start loadout wears the Common pair; upgrades add per level; the ring every hero wears starts empty
- `features/items/tests/test_rewards.gd`: Rewards: the first win pays everything and sets patrol_paid_<id>, a repeat win pays half the riyal and nothing else, herbs over the stack turn into riyal, the purse has a cap, a chest pays once
- `features/items/tests/test_shop.gd`: The herb stall: buy and sell rules and their edge cases (economy.md section 9), the ShopService purse signal, and using consumables in the field (FieldUse, ItemService)
- `features/jambiyah/defs/blade_def.gd`: A jambiyah blade: adds to attack, adds knockback to every hit the wielder lands, adds weight
- `features/jambiyah/defs/heirloom_def.gd`: Maps heirloom restoration rank to open stone slots and story flags (content/jambiyah/heirloom.json)
- `features/jambiyah/defs/hilt_def.gd`: A jambiyah hilt: adds to agility, multiplies cast speed, adds weight, and grants exactly one move
- `features/jambiyah/defs/loadout_def.gd`: A hero's starting gear: which weapon parts, prosthetic and accessory they own and wear at the start (each optional)
- `features/jambiyah/defs/stone_def.gd`: A gemstone socketed into a jambiyah hilt (content/jambiyah/stones.json)
- `features/jambiyah/logic/jambiyah.gd`: Builds Zayd's fighter from a base CombatantDef plus one hilt and one blade (docs/design/combat.md)
- `features/jambiyah/logic/loadout.gd`: Which gear a hero wears: the saved choice per slot ("<hero>.<part>" in GameState.equipment), else the starting gear
- `features/jambiyah/logic/stat_row.gd`: One line of the workshop comparison: label key, value now (base) and value with the chosen pair
- `features/jambiyah/logic/stones.gd`: Pure rules for jambiyah hilt gemstones: open socket counts, rarity fitting rules, and socket mutations
- `features/jambiyah/logic/workshop_stats.gd`: The comparison rows the equipment screen shows: base fighter against the fighter built by Jambiyah.equip
- `features/jambiyah/tests/test_jambiyah.gd`: T3: every hilt + blade pairing gives a different Zayd stat sets, inside the timeline caps; each hilt adds exactly one move; the shared base definition is never changed
- `features/jambiyah/tests/test_loadout.gd`: The loadout fallback: a hero wears the saved item per slot, else the start loadout

- `features/neon/battle/map_battle_events.gd`: purpose: Applies timeline events to actors and shown_hp (docs/design/first-playable.md section 3): damage numbers, hit freeze, KO pose on defeat, heals and revives, and reconciles shown_hp with the sim at the end of each batch

- `features/neon/battle/map_battle_vitals.gd`: purpose: Rydan's slanted Hades-like HP/SP bar bottom-left (docs/design/first-playable.md section 3): an ink border, a dark back, red HP above and teal SP below, both cut on the iso diagonal
- `features/neon/battle/tests/test_map_battle.gd`: purpose: MapBattle runs the real BattleSim on the map: an auto-choosing hero finishes the fight, `ended` fires once, the winner's living side stands and downed foes hold the ko; a melee hit applies only at the impact signal

- `features/neon/cold_open/neon_cold_open_def.gd`: purpose: The Roya cold open (content/neon/cold_open.json, docs/briefs/neon-cold-open.md): its painted shots (texture, seconds, caption key, slow push and pan, parallax layer), crossfade, caption, alert, cut, music and rain numbers

- `features/neon/defs/neon_room_def.gd`: One iso room (content/neon/rooms.json, docs/design/first-playable.md section 2): Feras's painted plate, the walkable outline and its holes, occluders cut from the plate (drawn over actors whose feet are above the baseline), the spawn, interactables, guard patrols, the room's encounter and the floodlight cone the fuse box kills
